verdicts.rationale: DEFECT CONFIRMED as Type2_PoorDiagnostics (revised from original 'behavior' type and 'High' severity to 'Medium' severity). Root cause: Milvus automatically creates a default index on vector fields during collection creation via the high-level API (REST v2 and pymilvus create_collection). When users attempt to create an explicit index, the system fails with the misleading error 'creating multiple indexes on same field is not supported'. This error is factually incorrect - the user is creating their FIRST explicit index, not 'multiple' indexes. The auto-created index is implicit behavior not documented in the REST API contract. Clean reproduction confirmed: (1) create_collection auto-creates index on 'vector' field, (2) explicit create_index fails with 'multiple indexes' error, (3) load_collection succeeds due to auto-index, (4) search succeeds using auto-index. Low-level API test confirmed load properly fails with 'index not found' when no index exists, validating the state constraint is enforced when truly applicable. Source code analysis (task.go:2243-2256) shows proper index checking logic, but the error message at index creation doesn't distinguish between explicit user-created indexes and auto-created indexes. The defect is in diagnostic quality: the error message should say 'Cannot create explicit index on field that already has an auto-created index. Use drop_index first to remove the auto-index' to guide users toward the solution. No data corruption or loss occurs - this is purely a UX/diagnostics issue affecting operational friction.
